title: Health Ministry Reassures No New Influenza Threat; H1N1 Shows Expected Seasonal Drift
summary: Union Health Ministry, along with DHR, ICMR, and NCDC, is closely monitoring seasonal respiratory illness trends nationwide through 73 DHR-ICMR Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDLs). DG ICMR Dr. Rajiv Bahl confirmed there is no cause for panic. Circulating Influenza A (H1N1) viruses have been identified as A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1) pdm09-like viruses. Hemagglutinin (HA) gene analysis places isolates in clade 6B.1A.5a2a, subclade D.3.1.1—a lineage in continuous circulation in India since 2025. Observed genetic changes reflect normal antigenic drift, not emergence of a new or dangerous strain. Genomic and epidemiological surveillance continues; seasonal influenza remains self-limiting. Authorities urged adherence to standard respiratory hygiene practices.

title: National Workshop on SSBSK Convenes to Strengthen Child Health with New Shaishav App
summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare held a two-day National Workshop on Samagra Shishu Bal Swasthya Karyakram (SSBSK) on August 24–25, 2026, at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra, chaired by Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, NHM. The workshop brought together State Nodal Officers for Child Health and ASHA from all 36 States/UTs to translate SSBSK Operational Guidelines into action, focusing on continuum of care for newborns and children up to three years. Key emphasis was placed on risk-differentiated care for early identification and intensified follow-up of at-risk newborns and children. The newly introduced Shaishav App was highlighted as a digital tool for tracking children, home visits, follow-ups, and referrals. The workshop aimed to strengthen digital monitoring and the continuum of care under SSBSK.

title: Government Bans Chlorpheniramine-Phenylephrine FDCs for Children Under 4 Years
summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has restricted the manufacture, sale, and distribution of all Fixed Dose Combinations (FDCs) containing Chlorpheniramine Maleate and Phenylephrine Hydrochloride for use in children below four years of age. The move follows recommendations of an Expert Committee and the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB), which noted potential risks to young children and availability of safer alternatives. This extends an earlier 15 April 2025 notification (S.O. 1717(E)) that restricted only certain FDCs with these ingredients; the latest order covers all formulations. Manufacturers must display the warning, "Fixed Dose Combination shall not be used in children below four years of age," on labels, package inserts, and promotional literature. Issued under Section 26A of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, the notification takes effect from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.

title: NLEP Review-cum-Capacity Building Workshop Held in Indore to Accelerate Leprosy Transmission Interruption
summary: The Central Leprosy Division, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, organized a two-day National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP) Review-cum-Capacity Building Workshop in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, on August 19, 2026. Over 70 participants attended, including the ADG (DGHS), DDG (Leprosy), officials from RLTRI Raipur and Aska Institute, State Leprosy Officers, CMHOs, and District Leprosy Officers from all 51 districts of Madhya Pradesh. The workshop reviewed the epidemiological situation, programme performance, and implementation gaps, emphasizing strengthening early case detection, contact tracing, timely treatment initiation and completion, prevention of disabilities, and intensified surveillance as key components of the last-mile strategy for Interruption of Transmission (IoT) of leprosy.

title: National Workshop on Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Convenes; New AMB Digital Platform Launched
summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare held a two-day National Workshop on Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (AMB) on August 12–13, 2026, in New Delhi, with over 160 participants from all States/UTs and representatives from the Ministries of Education, WCD, Panchayati Raj, Youth Affairs, and Tribal Affairs. Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava stressed stronger convergence across health programmes. A new AMB Digital Platform was launched to enable beneficiary-level tracking, treatment monitoring, and timely follow-up. The workshop focused on implementing the revised AMB Operational Guidelines (launched by Shri J.P. Nadda on 29 June 2026 at CCHFW), shifting from supplementation-focused to a comprehensive approach centered on testing, case-based management, treatment compliance, diverse diet, and digital tracking using the 7×7×7 strategy. States/UTs were also recognized for strong AMB performance.

title: Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Unveils 7X7X7 Framework with New Operational Guidelines
summary: Government of India released new Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (AMB) operational guidelines at the 16th Central Council of Health and Family Welfare (CCHFW) meeting on 29 June 2026, upgrading the strategy from 6X6X6 to 7X7X7. Key components: (1) Hb saturation testing using Digital Invasive Hemoglobinometers; (2) Prophylaxis and targeted therapeutic management by anemia category; (3) Segregation of nutritional and non-nutritional anemia for case-based management; (4) Shift from T3 (Test, Treat, Talk) to T4 (Test, Treat, Talk and Track) via robust digital tracking; (5) Dietary diversification through Eat Right Approach with locally available iron-rich foods; (6) Whole-of-Government convergent approach with inter-ministerial convergence; (7) Jan Bhagidari communication strategy for community ownership. The 7 beneficiary groups include children 6-59 months, 5-9 years, adolescents 10-19 years, pregnant women, lactating mothers, women of reproductive age (20-49 years), and 0-6 month LBW babies. The 7 interventions span prophylactic IFA supplementation, anemia testing, therapeutic management, and more.

title: Steps Taken to Promote Menstrual Health and Hygiene Under NHM
summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare implements the Menstrual Hygiene Scheme (MHS) under the National Health Mission (NHM) to promote menstrual hygiene among adolescent girls, with States/UTs supported based on proposals in their Annual Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs). MHS focuses on: (1) awareness generation; (2) access to quality and affordable sanitary napkins; (3) safe and environment-friendly disposal; and (4) counselling on safe menstrual practices. Sustained IEC activities are conducted through health facilities, community platforms, frontline health workers, digital dissemination, and adolescent-focused programme platforms. A Menstrual Hygiene Policy for school-going girls is implemented via coordinated State/UT action to ensure access to safe, effective, and affordable menstrual hygiene in schools. Monitoring under NHM is carried out through a multi-layered framework reviewing State-wise Key Deliverables against approved targets during NPCC meetings with all States/UTs. MHM is recognized as a multidimensional, inter-ministerial issue requiring coordinated action.

title: Update on Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme (PMNDP)
summary: The Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme (PMNDP) provides free haemodialysis to eligible patients via district hospital-based centres. As of 30.06.2026, PMNDP is operational in all 36 States/UTs, covering 751 districts (including 44 linked districts) through 1,856 haemodialysis centres equipped with 13,535 haemodialysis machines. State/UT proposals are considered in National Programme Coordination Committee (NPCC) meetings, with approvals conveyed through Records of Proceedings (RoPs). The Union Health Ministry undertakes periodic monitoring through the Common Review Mission (CRM) and visits by senior officers; non-operational centres are flagged to States/UTs for corrective action. PMNDP is supported under the National Health Mission (NHM) as a supplementary health subject. State-wise cumulative data on dialysis centres, including those added in the last two years, is annexed. Public health and hospitals remain State subjects, with GoI providing technical and financial support for dialysis infrastructure strengthening.

title: Government Steps to Reduce Out-of-Pocket Healthcare Expenditure
summary: India's MoHFW is reducing Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE) through multiple Centrally Sponsored Schemes. AB PM-JAY provides ₹5 lakh annual health cover to over 12 crore vulnerable families. Ayushman Vay Vandana covers 6 crore senior citizens aged 70+ irrespective of socio-economic status. A total of 1.87 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAM) have been operationalized for comprehensive primary healthcare including preventive, promotive, curative, palliative, and rehabilitative services. Free Drugs and Free Diagnostics Initiatives have been rolled out nationwide. Key schemes supporting affordable healthcare infrastructure include NHM, AB PM-JAY, PM-ABHIM (Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission), and PMSSY (Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana).

title: Initiatives for Care, Nutrition and Welfare of Pregnant Women
summary: Government initiatives under NHM ensure maternal healthcare, nutrition, and welfare for pregnant women. Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) provides completely free delivery (including C-section), drugs, diet, diagnostics, transport, and blood transfusion at public health institutions. Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) offers free quality antenatal check-ups by Specialists/Medical Officers on the 9th of every month. Extended PMSMA focuses on individual tracking of high-risk pregnant (HRP) women until safe delivery. Other key initiatives include SUMAN Roadmap 2030, Anaemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, Mission Saksham Anganwadi, and POSHAN 2.0. Implementation is supported by robust monitoring, technology-enabled governance, and community outreach for effective delivery of maternal health and nutrition benefits.

title: NHA Achieves 25 Crore OPD Registrations Milestone via ABHA Scan and Register Service
summary: The National Health Authority's Scan and Register Service (formerly Scan and Share Service), under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), has crossed 25 crore OPD registrations since its launch in October 2022. Nearly 4 lakh citizens use the service daily. The service is operational across 30,800 healthcare facilities in 36 States/UTs. Patients scan a unique QR code at facilities using any ABDM-enabled Personal Health Record (PHR) app, consent to share their ABHA profile, and complete instant OPD registration without paperwork. Leading adopters include Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, and Jammu & Kashmir. AIIMS New Delhi tops the country with over 54 lakh digital OPD registrations. The service significantly reduces waiting times and improves operational efficiency.

title: Government Strengthens Food Safety Enforcement with Expanded Testing Infrastructure
summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has outlined measures to strengthen food safety enforcement under the FSS Act, 2006. FSSAI has notified 259 NABL-accredited food testing laboratories, 24 referral labs, and 305 Mobile Testing Units (Food Safety on Wheels) for sample analysis. Under the SoFTeL (State of the Art Food Testing Laboratory) scheme, 47 State Food Testing Laboratories have been upgraded to enhance testing capacity. FSSAI regularly reviews the performance and vacancies of Food Safety Officers across States/UTs via Central Advisory Committee and Inter-State Zonal Council meetings. Consumer awareness initiatives include the DART (Detect Adulteration with Rapid Test) Book and Food Safety Magic Box, promoting adulteration detection and informed food choices. Implementation remains a shared responsibility between Central and State Governments.

title: Union Health Ministry Notifies Stricter Rules Against Fabricated Drug Data
summary: The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare has amended the Drugs Rules, 1945 (via G.S.R 756 (E), dated 16th October 2025) to enhance regulatory integrity. The Licensing Authority is now empowered to debar entities from filing further applications with State or Central regulatory authorities for a specified period if they submit fake or fabricated data. This adds to existing penalties like application rejection or license cancellation. The process includes a mandatory show-cause notice and a provision for appeal. The amendment aims to ensure drug quality, safety, and efficacy are based on reliable scientific evidence, deterring misconduct that poses risks to public health.

title: NJORT Deployed for Chandipura Virus Outbreak in Gujarat and Rajasthan
summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has deployed a National Joint Outbreak Response Team (NJORT) to Gujarat and Rajasthan to manage the Chandipura Virus Disease (CHPV) outbreak. The multidisciplinary team includes experts from NCDC, ICMR, and the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD). The response involves the activation of the NCDC Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) and continuous surveillance via the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP). Objectives include investigating transmission dynamics, clinical spectrum, epidemiology, and vector surveillance to guide evidence-based public health interventions.

title: Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission Recognized by WHO SEARN as Regional Centre of Excellence
summary: The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), under the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, was recognized by WHO SEARN as a Regional Centre of Excellence in Pharmacovigilance and Technical Centre in Quality of Medicines during SEARN's 10th Anniversary Meeting held in Kathmandu, Nepal, on 4–5 August 2026. SEARN, a WHO SEARO initiative established in 2016, brings together National Regulatory Authorities across the South-East Asia Region to strengthen regulatory systems through knowledge sharing, regulatory convergence, capacity building, and reliance mechanisms. Thematic working groups focus on quality assurance, pharmacovigilance, clinical trials oversight, regulatory preparedness, and medical device regulation. The IPC delegation was led by Dr. V. Kalaiselvan, Secretary-cum-Scientific Director, alongside Dr. Jai Prakash, Dr. Robin Kumar, and Mr. Arvind Kumar, showcasing India's regulatory excellence.

title: NFHS-6 Fact Sheet Indicators Finalized for Data Harmonization
summary: The Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) has finalized the indicators for the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6, 2023-24) National and State/UT Fact Sheets. In line with the Government of India's Data Harmonization initiative, the TAC focused on key health and family welfare indicators to reduce inconsistencies across official data sources. Notably, anaemia estimates will be released based on ICMR's 'Gold Standard' survey. The TAC included representatives from MoWCD, MoSPI, NITI Aayog, and the Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner of India.

title: ICMR i-DRONE Initiative Reduces TB Diagnosis Time and Cost
summary: An ICMR study on the i-DRONE initiative in Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri district, Telangana, demonstrates that drone-assisted transport of TB sputum samples significantly improves diagnostic efficiency in remote areas. In collaboration with AIIMS Bibinagar and the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP), the median turnaround time for diagnosis was reduced from 15 days to 5 days. Furthermore, mean out-of-pocket expenditure for patients decreased drastically from approximately ₹9,451 to ₹91, enhancing timely access to diagnostic services.

title: AB-PMJAY Impact and Expansion Update
summary: As of June 30, 2026, AB-PMJAY has authorized 12.69 crore cashless hospital admissions totaling ₹1.92 lakh crore across 37,413 hospitals. The scheme provides ₹5 lakh/family/year for secondary/tertiary care to the bottom 40% of the population. Key expansions include coverage for ~37 lakh ASHA/Anganwadi worker families (March 2024) and 6 crore senior citizens aged 70+ (October 2024), regardless of socio-economic status. National Health Accounts Estimates 2022-23 show a significant decline in out-of-pocket expenditure (OOPE) as a proportion of total health expenditure, dropping from 62.6% (2014-15) to 43.4% (2022-23). Card details are available at dashboard.nha.gov.in/public/card.

title: IPHS Digital Toolkit for Public Healthcare Assessment
summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare is utilizing an open-source toolkit and web-based dashboard (www.iphs.mohfw.gov.in), launched June 28, 2024, to monitor compliance with Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) 2022 across all facility levels, including Ayushman Arogya Mandirs. As of June 26, 2026, 100% of public healthcare facilities have been assessed through the IPHS Digital Toolkit, with 64% scoring above 50%. The system enables real-time updates and data-driven decision-making to identify gaps in staffing, equipment, and diagnostics in PHCs and CHCs. Rural health facility staffing details are available via the HDI 2023-24 report.
